snippet.title: The Rosenhan Experiment 😮😭
snippet.description:
What happened when 8 totally sane people were sent into an insane asylum?

In the 1970s, Stanford researchers sent eight completely healthy people into psychiatric hospitals to see if doctors could spot they were faking.

Each volunteer claimed to hear a single voice saying, “thud,” “empty,” or “hollow.” Which was enough to get them admitted.

Then the experiment really began.

Once inside, the volunteers acted completely normal.
No hallucinations. No strange behavior. Nothing.

But the doctors never changed their minds.
Every single volunteer was diagnosed with schizophrenia or manic depressive psychosis.

Some were locked inside for weeks. One stayed trapped for over 50 days.

Across 12 hospitals, not one staff member realized they were faking.
When Stanford published the results, psychiatry was shaken.

One hospital fought back and said,
“Send us your fake patients. We’ll catch them all.”

Over the next three months, they flagged 41 patients as impostors - and suspected 42 more.

But then Stanford revealed the twist. 
They hadn't sent a single fake patient at all.

snippet.title: 100 Impossible Paradoxes That Break the Fabric of Time to Fall Asleep To

In this Sleep or Think session, we invite you to spend 3 quiet hours with 100 impossible paradoxes that break the fabric of time, logic, and reality itself — not through confusion, but through the calm, mind-bending recognition that the universe contains questions so perfectly constructed that answering them only creates deeper questions. From a grandfather paradox that makes time travel logically self-destroying, to a bootstrap paradox where information exists with no origin, from Schrödinger's cat that is simultaneously alive and dead until observed, to Roko's Basilisk — a thought experiment so disturbing that simply knowing it exists changes your relationship to the future, each paradox unfolds gently and clearly.

Let these impossible puzzles reshape how you see time, causality, identity, and the strange realization that logic itself has edges where it quietly breaks down and stops working — perfect for late-night wonder, deep reflection, or simply to fall asleep to the soft rhythm of thoughtful narration.

At Sleep or Think, we're building a quiet space for curious minds — a place to learn, rest, and drift through the paradoxes that have kept philosophers, physicists, and mathematicians awake for centuries. If you find comfort here, consider joining us.

snippet.description:
About 2 to 4% of people experience something called synesthesia.

Synesthesia is when the brain blends senses that are normally separate.

Some people see colors when they hear music.
Others taste flavors when they read words

Interestingly, synesthesia appears very often among highly creative musicians.

Artists like Kanye West, Pharrell Williams, Billie Eilish, and Lady Gaga have all described seeing or feeling music as colors, textures, or shapes.

snippet.title: Why do we use "they" as a singular pronoun? - Arika Okrent
snippet.description:
Take a look at 3 English language grammar rules to find out where they come from and if you actually need to follow them.

--

Grammatical rules have caused heated debate in various regions and languages for centuries. But while we know people take grammar seriously, what’s less clear is, why? Where do these seemingly random rules come from, and which, if any, actually matter? Arika Okrent takes a closer look at three famous examples from the English language that have been the source of numerous grammatical arguments.

snippet.title: Supervolcano That Once Changed the Planet Is Waking Up
snippet.description:
A supervolcano responsible for one of the most powerful eruptions in human history is showing signs of renewed activity after more than 7,000 years. Scientists studying Japan’s Kikai Caldera have found evidence that the massive volcanic system is slowly refilling with magma, rebuilding beneath the seafloor since its catastrophic eruption around 7,300 years ago. That ancient event released enormous amounts of ash and volcanic material, altering regional environments and leaving a lasting mark on Earth's geological history. While researchers do not expect an eruption anytime soon, the discovery offers a rare opportunity to observe how supervolcanoes recover and evolve over thousands of years. Join us as we explore what scientists have found beneath Kikai Caldera, why it matters, and what it reveals about the future of one of the planet’s most powerful volcanic systems.

snippet.title: What causes avalanches, and can you survive them? - Simon Trautman
snippet.description:
Explore the three conditions needed to trigger an avalanche, and what makes these natural disasters so hard to survive.

--

Avalanches are the rapid descent of snow, ice, rock, or a combination of these down a slope. They can be destructive natural disasters and personal tragedies: killing an average of 27 people annually in the US. These alpine nightmares don’t just awaken out of nowhere; they need three specific conditions. So, what causes an avalanche? And is there any way to survive? Simon Trautman investigates.

localized.title: What causes avalanches, and can you survive them? - Simon Trautman
localized.description:
Explore the three conditions needed to trigger an avalanche, and what makes these natural disasters so hard to survive.

--

Avalanches are the rapid descent of snow, ice, rock, or a combination of these down a slope. They can be destructive natural disasters and personal tragedies: killing an average of 27 people annually in the US. These alpine nightmares don’t just awaken out of nowhere; they need three specific conditions. So, what causes an avalanche? And is there any way to survive? Simon Trautman investigates.

snippet.title: Voyager 1 Found a Wall at the Edge of Our Solar System
snippet.description:
Voyager 1 has been traveling through space since 1977 and is now far beyond the planets of our Solar System. But what it recently sent back surprised scientists. At the very edge of the Solar System, in a region known as the heliopause, Voyager 1 detected something unexpected - a highly energetic boundary zone that behaves nothing like the calm “edge of space” scientists once imagined. Instead, it appears to be a violent region of particle collisions and extreme energy.

snippet.title: 6 Scariest Space Phenomena That Will Terrify You
snippet.description:
